findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator negative-offset slicing crashes on Django querysets
findings.body: When `enable_advanced_features` is true and `cursor.offset < 0`, the code does `queryset[start_offset:stop]` with a negative `start_offset`. Django ORM querysets do not support negative slicing and raise `AssertionError: Negative indexing is not supported`. So the advertised 'advanced' negative-offset pagination path will 500 on the first request that uses a negative-offset cursor, rather than return data. The comment claiming 'the underlying Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically' is factually wrong.

findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator get_item_key breaks on datetime sort keys used by the audit logs endpoint
findings.body: `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key` does `int(math.floor(value))` on the attribute named by `self.key`, which is a copy of the numeric `Paginator` implementation. However, `OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint` (organization_auditlogs.py line 79) instantiates it with `order_by="-datetime"` where `AuditLogEntry.datetime` is a datetime. `math.floor(datetime)` raises TypeError, and `value_from_cursor` returns the raw cursor value (an epoch-ms int) which is then compared against the datetime column in `build_queryset`. This is exactly why `DateTimePaginator` exists (strftime conversion and multiplier-based `value_from_cursor`). Any request with `optimized_pagination=true` will fail with a 500.

findings.title: BasePaginator silently clamps negative forward-cursor offsets to 0, returning wrong page
findings.body: The change `start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset` means a client-supplied next cursor with a negative offset (e.g. the string `0:-5:0`) is silently clamped to 0 and returns the first page instead of erroring. Combined with the new comment in cursors.py claiming negative offsets are a supported 'performance optimization', this creates an undocumented, unvalidated path where malformed/hostile cursors produce incorrect pagination results without any error. Offsets should be validated (rejected) rather than silently clamped, and the `is_prev` branch still passes negative offsets straight into queryset slicing, which raises Django's negative-indexing AssertionError.

findings.title: Redirect-follow loop depth silently reduced from 10000 to 1000
findings.body: The redirect loop bound was cut from 10000 to 1000 with the explanatory comment ('theoretically this limit means that segment trees of depth 10k may not be joined together correctly') removed. For traces whose redirect chains exceed 1000 hops, the loop exits without finding the terminal set key; the script then writes `hset(main_redirect_key, span_id, set_span_id)` with the non-final `set_span_id`, permanently corrupting the redirect map and causing those spans to be buffered (and later flushed) under the wrong segment, splitting traces. If the reduction is intentional it needs justification and a metric/alarm; the original comment documenting the failure mode was deleted.

findings.title: Hardcoded eviction cap of 1000 inconsistent with SpansBuffer.max_segment_spans and not configurable
findings.body: The Lua script hardcodes `if span_count > 1000 then zpopmin(...)` while the Python `SpansBuffer` still exposes `max_segment_spans: int = 1001` (buffer.py line 150), and the Python-side enforcement in `_load_segment_data` was removed. The two limits disagree by one and the Lua value cannot be changed without redeploying the script; any config change to `max_segment_spans` in Python now has no effect. The cap should be passed in via ARGV (like `set_timeout`) so both sides stay consistent, and the unused/dead `max_segment_spans` parameter should be reconciled.

findings.title: Eviction via zpopmin can silently drop the root span while hrs flag persists
findings.body: When a set exceeds 1000 members, `zpopmin` removes the spans with the smallest `end_timestamp_precise` scores. If the root/segment span happens to be among the evicted spans, it is silently dropped, but the `span-buf:hrs:` flag for the set remains set (and is refreshed at line 69). The segment will then be flushed after the shorter root timeout with no root span present, producing a segment whose `is_segment` marker is never set for any span — downstream consumers that rely on exactly one segment span per segment will see malformed output. There is no guard to keep the root span (e.g. by score or by member check) during eviction.

findings.title: Undocumented public query parameter switches paginator implementation
findings.body: A new `optimized_pagination=true` request parameter silently changes the pagination behavior (cursor semantics, response cursor format) of an experimental but public API endpoint, with no documentation, no test coverage, and no serialization/schema change. Because `OptimizedCursorPaginator` has different cursor value encoding than `DateTimePaginator`, cursors obtained from one mode are invalid in the other, so a client toggling the flag mid-pagination will get wrong results. The feature flag should be documented and the parameter validated, or the paginator choice should be made server-side only.

findings.title: No tests for OptimizedCursorPaginator or the negative-offset path
findings.body: The new `OptimizedCursorPaginator` class and the modified offset handling in `BasePaginator.get_result` (line 182) have zero test coverage in this PR. Both contain the crash-producing paths described above (negative slicing assertion, datetime key TypeError), which any basic unit test exercising them would have caught. Tests should cover: normal forward/backward paging, negative offsets with and without `enable_advanced_features`, and datetime sort keys.
